key_insight: Dialogue re-cinematography turns a single wide-angle recording into multiple cinematic views. The central idea is to use audio alongside visual cues to guide speaking motion when the original footage provides little lip detail.
problem_solved: Filming close-ups, medium shots, and over-the-shoulder views is costly. Synthesizing these views from one recording is an alternative, but visual-only generators struggle with lip motion when faces are small or poorly visible.
method: Use a single wide-angle dialogue video as the source for additional shots.
Ground shot synthesis in dialogue audio rather than relying only on visible facial motion.
Target alternative cinematic framings with speech-consistent lip motion; implementation details are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: Audio grounding offers a way to make generated dialogue shots more faithful to speech while reducing the need for multi-camera coverage. For practitioners, the paper highlights audio as a useful signal when visual evidence is weak.
visual_elements: One wide-angle source frame branching into close-up, medium, and over-the-shoulder views.
A pipeline diagram showing source video plus audio feeding a shot-synthesis model.
An audio waveform aligned with a sequence of mouth movements.
A conceptual comparison of visual-only versus audio-grounded generation when the source face is small.
paper_title: One Take, Many Cameras: Audio-Grounded Shot Synthesis for Dialogue Re-Cinematography
paper_authors: Anthony Chen, Naomi Ken Korem, Matan Ben-Yosef, Tavi Halperin, Urska Jelercic
